 Order

This is the second application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of the BNSS, 2023 for grant of bail relating to Crime No.175 of 2024 registered at Police Station Kailaras, District Morena (M.P.)
for the offence under Sections 366, 363, 376, 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC and Section 4, 5, 6 of POCSO Act.
First application was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to file fresh after filing of charge sheet by this Court vide order dated 30.07.2024 in M.Cr.C.No.26161 of 2024.
Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant is innocent person and has been falsely implicated.
It is further submitted that the applicant is under custody since 01.06.2024.
After completion of investigation, charge sheet has already been filed, therefore, his custodial interrogation is not required anymore.
Further submission is that the entire posecution story is highly suspicious in the light of the fact that allegedly the prosecutrix got missing on 13.04.2024 and was recovered on 30.05.2024.

After her recovery, in her first NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:15702 2 MCRC-34261-2024 statement recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. on 30.05.2024 and Section 164 of Cr.P.C. on 31.05.2024, she has not corroborated the prosecution story, however, in her second statement recorded on 22.06.2024, for the first time, she made Babulal Gurjar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118772815/

sentences.text: It is further argued that even in her second statement, the prosecutrix stated that she left her house because she wanted to marry with the co-accused Krishna.
Allegation of rape is not on the applicant/accused.
The applicant is having age of 52 years.
Seizure of all documents has already been done.
Futher submission is that the applicant is having no criminal antecedents.
The applicant is permanent resident of District Morena.
Conclusion of trial is likely to take time and there is no possibility of his absconsion, if release on bail.
On these grounds, he prays for grant of bail to the applicant.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor for respondent/State as well as the counsel for the complainant vehemently opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the case diary available on record.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lac Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court.
Learned State counsel is directed to send an e-copy of this order to the Station House Officer of the concerned Police Station for information and necessary action.
E- copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance, if possible, by the office of this Court.
